title: Strided KV shape sensitivity across Llama/Mistral/Qwen (long-context & MoE routing interactions)
content:
Purpose:
Quick notes from a mid-iteration investigation into how strided/unaligned KV shapes and attention stride patterns affect runtime performance across Llama, Mistral, and Qwen families, with a focus on long-context workloads and interactions with MoE routing (gating + expert dispatch). Goal is to capture observed bottlenecks, heuristics that reproduce problems, and recommended mitigations to try in the next sprint.

Summary of key findings (high level):
- Unaligned KV tensor shapes (N, S, H) layouts with non-contiguous strides cause >20-35% slowdowns in attention kernels on A100/RTX series for certain model variants (Qwen especially sensitive).
- Mistral's chunked rotary offsets expose a pathological cache write pattern: alternating small writes lead to high cudaMemcpy stalls and fragmented device-side allocator behavior under heavy long-context traffic.
- Llama quantized kernels (4/8-bit) handle contiguous KV nicely, but when we pack batched sequences with variable lengths into a single buffer (to save memory), attention kernel selects slower fallback code paths.
- MoE routing aggravates the issue: uneven expert selection creates small per-expert micro-batches that then produce many small scatter/gather ops (gather_experts, scatter_grads) whose overhead dominates when sequence lengths are large.

Experiment matrix (what we ran):
- Models: Llama-2-13B (fp16 & q4f16), Mistral-7B (fp16), Qwen-7B (fp16)
- Workloads: long-context synthetic (1k/4k/8k token prefixes), conversational mixes (avg len 512, 90th 2k), MoE toy model with 64 experts, top-2 gating
- Hardware: NV A100 80GB (latest drivers), RTX6000 Ada, 32-core CPU hosts (non-NUMA tuned), 100Gbps host network disabled (single-node runs)
- Tools: Nsight Systems sampling (10k samples), CUPTI kernel timelines, nvprof-style flamegraphs, lightweight in-process spans (tracing hooks), and our rttrace end-to-end latency traces

Representative perf numbers (median of 3 runs):
- Llama-2-13B, 4k context, fp16 contiguous KV: p50 generation latency per token = 18ms, p99 = 42ms, GPU mem delta per request = 1.9GB
- Llama-2-13B, 4k context, packed variable-length KV (non-contiguous): p50 = 24ms (+33%), p99 = 59ms (+40%), GPU mem delta = 1.7GB (lower but more alloc churn)
- Mistral-7B, 8k context, typical rotary-chunk offsets: p50 = 26ms, p99 = 72ms; observed many cudaMemcpyAsync wait stalls coinciding with small KV writes
- Qwen-7B, 4k context, non-aligned KV layout (shifted by 128 bytes): end-to-end p50 +38%, kernel-level slowdown in scaled-dot-product attention ~2.1x for some shapes
- MoE toy, 1k context, 64 experts, top-2: average per-expert micro-batch size 4-8 tokens -> router_forward and gather_experts become ~45% of compute time vs ~12% for uniform selection

Profiling traces and hotspots (observations):
- compute_attention.* (device kernels) increased wall time when input stride != expected. Kernel launch heuristics fell back to slower tiling strategy based on shape heuristics in fused-attn kernels.
- kv_cache_write / kv_cache_alloc: many small allocations/writes in Mistral flows. Device allocator fragmentation prominent (cudaMallocAsync not pooling due to shape mismatches).
- gather_experts / scatter_outputs: excessive small memcpy patterns for MoE; CPU->GPU enqueue overhead visible in trace.
- host->device transfers: more frequent but smaller transfers when buffer packing logic attempts to compress variable-length sequences. This increased PCIe latency visibility on RTX series.
- dispatcher lock contention on CPU when building per-expert batches (thread pool exhaustion at high concurrency).

Hypotheses (why this is happening):
1) Kernel path selection depends on stride/alignment heuristics. When shapes don’t match the fast path (expected contiguous layouts), we hit broadly-tested but suboptimal kernels.
2) Rotary/position encoding chunking used by Mistral modifies memory access patterns making writes smaller and less coalesced, hurting bandwidth-bound kernels.
3) MoE gating causes fragmentation of work: many small dispatches reduce amortization of kernel launch and memcpy cost.
4) Our on-the-fly packing for variable lengths reduces memory but increases allocator churn and small-copy overhead, which hurts long-context throughput.

Immediate mitigations tried (and results):
- Force contiguous KV buffers at packing step: eliminated allocator churn, p50 improved back to within 5-7% of contiguous baseline, but increased peak memory by ~12%. Trade-off: memory vs latency.
- Grouped expert dispatching: hold routing results for 2-3 micro-batches and combine per-expert queues to increase micro-batch sizes -> reduced gather_experts overhead by ~30% and improved p99 by ~18% on MoE runs. Introduces up to 5-8ms extra queuing delay in tail; acceptable for throughput-oriented workloads.
- Kernel hinting: patch fused-attn scheduler to prefer a different tile size for shapes with stride > 1. Small gains (~6-10%) on Qwen tests. Needs broader validation.
- Pre-allocated KV arenas per-request size class: avoided frequent small allocations; reduced device allocator stalls but requires careful memory cap accounting.

Longer-term mitigations to explore:
- Implement shape-normalization layer: on input, reshape/copy KV into canonical contiguous layout only when it would cause a kernel fallback. Use a cheap heuristic to decide when to normalize to avoid unnecessary copies.
- Kernel autotuning stage on first N requests: collect shape stats and pre-select best kernel variant for those shapes (persist per-model/per-instance).
- MoE batching policy: smarter routing buffer that can opt between lower latency (immediate dispatch) and higher throughput (buffer + combine) based on realtime SLO budgets.
- Device-side aggregator for small gathers: implement a single fused kernel that accepts many small gather indexes to reduce host->device hop count.
- Rotary-aware KV packing for Mistral: detect chunk offset pattern and write larger contiguous chunks to avoid small cudaMemcpy calls.

Open questions / unknowns to validate:
- How much of Qwen sensitivity is due to model layer sizes (head dim alignments) vs implementation-specific tensor strides? Need to instrument lower-level tensor metadata.
- Does our CUDA allocator version (driver+cuda runtime) significantly change fragmentation behavior for small writes? Re-run on NGC images with different allocators.
- Can we safely increase prefetch window for KV caching when routing is active without blowing memory budgets?

Next steps (recommended short sprint items):
1) Add shape-normalization fast-path (small copy) guarded by a heuristic; measure p95/p99 on the three model families. (Owner: Priya)
2) Prototype per-expert combine buffer in routing module (Owner: Liam) — aim to make combine optional via config flag.
3) Run full autotune job (10k request simulation) to choose fused-attn tile sizes for Qwen; log decisions into model profile metadata. (Owner: Melody)
4) Re-run key experiments on 2 additional host images (CUDA 12.1 / 12.3) and document allocator behavior (Owner: Infra team request).

Notes for docs / runbook updates:
- Add a section into serving runtime runbook titled "KV shape sensitivity" with simple rules: prefer contiguous layout for long-context; enable expert-combine when MoE tail latency not critical; watch allocator churn metrics (gpu_alloc_wait_ms).
- Track a gating metric: fraction of requests that hit slower attention kernel path. Create alert if >5% for production models with >1k context.

Appendix (raw trace snippets and grep keys):
- trace keys: compute_attention:tileFallback, kv_cache:smallWrite, router:smallDispatch, cudaMemcpy:scatterCount>64
- example flame: /tmp/nvflame_run_20241110.svg (attached to linked PR)
- quick grep command used: rg "tileFallback|smallWrite|gather_experts" -n traces/*.trace

Unresolved tradeoffs:
- Memory vs latency: normalizing to contiguous layout fixes latency but raises memory. For Hosted API we should probably prefer latency for real-time endpoints and memory for batch endpoints. Need a config knob surfaced in model profile.
- Complexity vs benefit: device-side aggregator is non-trivial but could substantially reduce host-device roundtrips for MoE. Evaluate cost.

If you're reading this and have extra traces, drop them in the linked PR or add to JIRA INF-2418.

-- Priya
